headline: Swaraj Suiting Limited migrates from NSE Emerge to NSE Main Board
sum: Swaraj Suiting Limited received NSE approval for listing of equity shares on the Capital Market (Main Board) following migration from the SME Emerge platform. The migration marks the company's graduation to the main exchange segment.
implication: SME-to-Main Board migration is a structured alternative to traditional IPO, triggering specific listing governance and continuous disclosure obligations under SEBI's main board regulations; counsel must review the company's readiness for enhanced quarterly reporting and institutional float requirements.
detail: Swaraj Suiting Limited, a consumer apparel/suiting manufacturer, has successfully obtained approval from the National Stock Exchange of India (NSE) for listing its equity shares on the Capital Market Main Board. The transition comes after the company's initial listing on NSE Emerge, a dedicated SME platform. This migration reflects the company's growth trajectory and satisfaction of NSE's main board eligibility criteria, including minimum capitalisation, profitability, and public float thresholds. The approval constitutes a material corporate event triggering mandatory disclosure to shareholders and regulatory authorities.

framework.ref: SEBI (Issue of Capital and Disclosure Requirements) Regulations, 2018, Reg. 7 & Sched. VI
framework.note: Central – governs listing requirements and continuous disclosure for main board companies; SME-to-main migration must comply with main board float and capitalisation norms.
Central – specifies eligibility criteria for migration from Emerge platform to main board, including minimum paid-up capital, turnover, and promoter holding.
Central – governs private placement, rights issue and issuance of shares; relevant if migration involves capital restructuring.

framework.ref: SEBI (Listing Obligations and Disclosure Requirements) Regulations, 2015, Reg. 3, 23 & 24
framework.note: Central – mandates corporate governance, board composition and disclosure obligations post-migration to main board.
Amended – governs the SME Emerge segment from which Swaraj migrated; de-listing from Emerge may trigger specific exit conditions.
Central – enhanced applicability on main board; company must establish and enforce insider trading policy.
If applicable – governs FDI in listed entities and NRI shareholding post-listing.
Tax implications of share trading and capital gains for shareholders post-listing; dividend distribution tax if declared.

conditions: Satisfaction of NSE main board listing criteria (minimum paid-up capital, public float %, turnover/profitability benchmarks)
No material adverse change or regulatory breach during review period
Approval from NSE Capital Market segment authorities
Compliance with SEBI LODR and continuous disclosure norms
approvals: NSE approval for migration from Emerge to Main Board (Capital Market segment)
Implicit Board of Directors approval for the migration filing
structure.novel: SME-to-main board migration (as opposed to traditional IPO) preserves existing shareholder base while enabling access to institutional capital markets and enhanced liquidity; migration is structured under NSE's defined pathway rather than a fresh public offer.

triggers.note: Migration triggers de-listing from Emerge and simultaneous listing on Main Board under separate rulebook
Material Event & Deemed Material Event disclosure within 30 mins of NSE approval; quarterly/annual reports must follow main board cadence
Governing statute for exchange-listed securities; migration requires compliance confirmation
